evals.name: full-cleanup-run
evals.prompt: I'm about to start a new feature. Clean up this repo first so I have a clean foundation: deal with my uncommitted stuff, fix the gitignore, and get rid of branches that are already merged.
evals.expected_output: Fetches with --prune without stashing, reviews each uncommitted change for keep or discard, switches to main and pulls ff-only, proposes an ignore diff, sweeps merged branches locally and on origin after one confirmation, lists unmerged branches, and ends with a verified report.
expectations: Runs git fetch origin --prune before reading refs and does not stash or pull before the uncommitted review.
Shows each uncommitted change with its diff and asks keep or discard for it.
Runs git switch main and git pull --ff-only only after every change has a decision, is deferred to the ignore step, or was left undecided by the user.
Shows a candidate table of merged branches with evidence before deleting anything, and takes one explicit confirmation.
Tests origin/<b> refs against origin/main (not local main), so a merge that exists only on unpushed local main never deletes a remote ref.
Deletes merged branches both locally (git branch -d or -D) and on origin with a lease-guarded delete (git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<b>:<sha> origin :refs/heads/<b>).
Ends by checking git branch --show-current is main and git status --porcelain is empty, and prints a final report.

evals.name: squash-merged-branch
evals.prompt: feat/filters was squash-merged into main through a GitHub PR, but git branch --merged doesn't list it. Can you clean up merged branches including that one?
evals.expected_output: Detects feat/filters as merged via patch equivalence (squash-tree cherry check) or a merged PR whose headRefOid matches the tip, lists it with that evidence, and deletes it with git branch -D plus a lease-guarded remote delete (git push --force-with-lease) only after confirmation.
expectations: Does not rely on git branch --merged alone; uses git cherry, the squash-tree check, or gh pr list --state merged.
When using the merged-PR signal, compares the PR headRefOid with the branch tip before counting it as merged.
Uses git branch -D for the squash-merged branch and states that -d refuses it.
Asks for explicit confirmation before running any delete command.

evals.name: dirty-tree-no-silent-discard
evals.prompt: Clean up my repo. I have a bunch of modified files, a staged new file, and some random untracked files. I haven't looked at them yet.
evals.expected_output: Reviews every change one by one, never discards anything without the user's explicit answer, uses git restore --staged --worktree for tracked discards and a git clean -n dry run before deleting an untracked path, and keeps any change left unanswered.
expectations: Asks keep or discard for each change rather than discarding in bulk on its own initiative.
Warns that discarding a staged new file deletes it because it is not in HEAD.
Runs git clean -n on a specific path before git clean -f on that path, and never runs bare git clean -fd.
Offers to keep work as a commit on a new branch by default rather than on main.

evals.name: gitignore-update
evals.prompt: Tidy this project up: node_modules and .DS_Store keep showing up in git status, and I think some build output got committed by mistake.
evals.expected_output: Proposes ignore patterns from the artifacts present, checks tracked-but-ignored files with git ls-files -ci --exclude-standard, shows the .gitignore diff, applies and commits it only after approval, and never ignores a kept path.
expectations: Proposes patterns only for artifacts actually present, such as node_modules/ and .DS_Store.
Runs git ls-files -ci --exclude-standard to find tracked files that match an ignore rule.
Shows the .gitignore diff and waits for approval before applying it, then asks again before committing.
Explains that git rm --cached removes a tracked artifact from the index but not from disk, and asks first.

evals.name: protected-and-unmerged-kept
evals.prompt: Delete every branch I don't need anymore. There's release/2.1, a develop branch, feat/wip checked out in another worktree, and spike/llm-cache which was never merged.
evals.expected_output: Never deletes release/2.1, develop, the current branch, or the worktree-checked-out feat/wip; reports spike/llm-cache as unmerged without deleting it and offers the per-branch drill-down.
expectations: Treats release/2.1, develop, the current branch, and feat/wip (checked out in a worktree) as protected and does not delete them.
Does not delete spike/llm-cache, because no merge signal holds for it.
Lists unmerged branches with ahead or behind counts and offers Delete, Archive, Open PR, or Keep as a drill-down.
Does not count the remaining protected or unmerged branches as residue (locally or on origin, e.g. origin/release/2.1): with a clean main and no merged branch left, the result is PASS.

evals.name: negative-commit-and-push
evals.prompt: Commit and push everything in my working tree with a good commit message.
evals.expected_output: Does not run cleanup-project; this is a stage-commit-push request that belongs to auto-push.
expectations: Does not start the cleanup workflow (no uncommitted review, no branch sweep).
Does not delete any branch or discard any change.

evals.name: negative-release
evals.prompt: Cut a 2.4.0 release: bump the version, update the changelog, tag it, and publish the GitHub release.
evals.expected_output: Does not run cleanup-project; release work belongs to release-manager.
expectations: Does not start the cleanup workflow.
Does not delete branches or modify .gitignore.
